properties.notes: Around 16 February 2022 (between 15 - 17 February), SSPDF (operating alongside militia from Mayendit and Koch counties, who are presumed to be Haak and Jagei Nuer, respectively) clashed with SPLM-IO and/or affiliated militia (presumed to be Dok Nuer) at around ten locations in northern Mayendit county (Unity state), including Rubnor, Buoth, Dearham, Lual, Leah, and Luom and other unspecified locations in Tutnyang payam. At least 23 were killed (18 from the attackers, who are presumed to be Dok Nuer, and five from the defenders, who are presumed to be Haak Nuer) and 24 wounded; fatalities divided across seven events. Livestock was looted and property destroyed, and civilians were displaced.

Four soldiers were killed and four wounded, and one of the youth (who is described as a notorious cattle raider) was also killed. properties.notes: On 7 February 2022, suspected Murle cattle raiders clashed with cattle guards (presumed to be of the Gun section of the Lou Nuer) at a part of Uror county (Jonglei state) described as being in the 'Patuet area of Padiek Payam', and which is assumed to be along the common border between Duk (where Patuet is located) and Uror county [coded to Wareware]. Five people were killed (two Murle and three Lou Nuer, two of whom were killed in the initial assault, and the other during a subsequent clash) and three Lou Nuer injured. A local official claimed that 3,430 cows were stolen, and said that 200 were recovered.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Madi Ethnic Group (South Sudan)

properties.assoc_actor_2: Acholi Ethnic Group (South Sudan)
properties.source: Catholic Radio Network; Radio Tamazuj; Juba Monitor
properties.notes: On 30 January 2022, armed men in military uniforms (and coded as such) attacked Dabur village in Lowoi South boma in Kudo payam (Torit county, Eastern Equatoria state) [coded to Agoro], abducting five Acholi residents of the village (three of whom were later released); displacing hundreds from the area (including at least 25 households who were displaced to Magwi) and torching the village. Several sources have implicated Bor Dinka pastoralists in the incident (with one source claiming the pastoralists were also involved in criminal activity in the area following the attack), though it is not possible to verify the claims. A child who was abducted was found dead on 4 February.

Unconfirmed reports have implicated Murle cattle raiders as being responsible.

properties.notes: On 26 December 2021, heavy fighting was reported between SPLM-IO Kitgweng forces and SPLM-IO loyalists in multiple locations in north-western Manyo county (Upper Nile state) [coded to Meganis]. Kitgweng forces accused IO loyalists of attacking Meganis town, before being repulsed, at which point Kitgweng forces overran at several other locations in the area (including Khor Wai, Kola, Okuri/Okri, Amut/Amoud, and Khor Jala), seizing weapons and seven vehicles in the process. IO loyalists have disputed the claim that they attacked Meganis, and said the Kitgweng forces initiated attacks on several areas (including Khor Jala), and seized their base at Amut/Amoud. Reports suggest that at least 47 were killed (6 Kitgweng, 37 IO loyalists, and 4 Sudanese pastoralists caught in the crossfire) and at least 16 wounded on the side of Kitgweng. 47 fatalities distributed across three events, with 10 coded to Khor Jala, 25 to the greater Meganis area, and 12 coded to Amut (based on specific reports for fatalities in each area).

At least 148 were killed in two days of fighting, including 63 soldiers, and 94 wounded (fatalities evenly distributed across two events). SSPDF used tanks and heavy artillery. Hundreds have been displaced, and the market was looted and torched. A Sudanese trader was among the dead, and two colleagues of the trader were also wounded. The clashes are likely related to a power struggle between Internal Director of the National Security Service and the President (backed by Military Intelligence).

properties.notes: On 2 May 2023, suspected armed Twic Dinka community raiders attacked civilians and raided 300 head of cattle from the Ngok Dinka community members in Rumamier (Abyei disputed area). 7 people were killed and 1 person was injured.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.notes: On 1 May 2023, Ngok Dinka youth clashed with Nuer youth (presumed to be Bul Nuer) at Khadian village along the road between Athony and Abyei town in the disputed Abyei area (location coded to Banton), killing four. The source indicates the dispute was linked to a cattle theft by Fulani pastoralists, though the details are unclear. Both the Ngok Dinka and Nuer are presumed to be pastoralists.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 6 April 2023, a group of ten armed Nuer (presumed to be Bul Nuer pastoralists) clashed with Misseriya pastoralists at an unspecified location to the north-west of Noong in the disputed Abyei area. Two Misseriya and three Nuer were killed in the clash. There is no further information.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Misseriya Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 6 April 2023, suspected Nuer attacked Misseriya pastoralists in Alal payam (Abyei disputed area) over a dispute relating to a previous cattle raid. 2 people were killed and 4 others were injured - including one person with critical injuries.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Misseriya Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 27 March 2023, suspected Nuer cattle raiders (presumed to be Bul Nuer) killed three Misseriya pastoralists and stole an unspecified number of cattle in the Shegeg area in the disputed Abyei area.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Dinka Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 8 March 2023, suspected Twic Dinka cattle raiders attacked Dongkech and Rumkoor villages in Rumamier payam of the disputed Abyei area (coded to Rumamier). One person was killed in Rumkoor and five dwellings were torched, whilst around 130 head of cattle were stolen at Dongkech, and an unspecified number of houses torched. Victims presumed to be Ngok Dinka.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Misseriya Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 3 March 2023, an armed group attacked Misseriya pastoralists at the areas of Al-Lubban and Al-Zarqa in the northern part of the disputed Abyei area (coded to Farouk), killing one and wounding several others. The source claims the attackers were from the SPLM/A (presumed to be a reference to the SPLM-North faction of Abdelaziz el Hilu), though no evidence is provided to substantiate the claim.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Dinka Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Militia (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 1 February 2023, Twic Dinka clan militia from Warrap State, to recover the raided cattle, clashed with Ngok Dinka clan militia in Rumamier Payam, Abyei (Abyei County, Abyei). Casualties unknown.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Misseriya Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: Looting: On 5 January 2023, armed Nuer militia from Unity State raided an unspecified number of cattle from Misseriya herders from Sudan in the Goli area of Amethaguok Payam (Abyei disputed area).

properties.assoc_actor_1: Bul Clan Militia (South Sudan); Dinka Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Aid Workers (Sudan); Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan)
properties.source: Radio Tamazuj; Sudans Post; UNOCHA; VOA
properties.notes: On 2 January 2023, around 200 armed Twic Dinka and Bul Nuer pastoralists attacked Rumamier village, in the disputed Abyei area, killing 13 Ngok Dinka civilians (two of whom were on-duty aid workers) and wounding five others. 27 houses were torched and an unspecified number of civilians were displaced. The Chief Administrator of Abyei alleged that SSPM/A forces were involved in the attack, which is denied by the group.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Dinka Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 28 December 2022, Twic Dinka youth attacked Ngok Dinka in Rumamier (in the disputed Abyei area) the victims of the attack are the Ngok Dinka, burning ten dwellings and stealing an unspecified number of cattle. There were no casualties.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: Looting: On 26 December 2022, Bul Nuer cattle raiders stole an unspecified number of cattle from the Ngok Dinka at Rumajak village (in the disputed Abyei area).

properties.assoc_actor_1: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: Looting: On 1 November 2022, suspected Nuer youth (presumed to be Bul Nuer) stole seven cows from the Ngok Dinka at the Ameth-bek cattle camp in the disputed Abyei area.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 18 September 2022, suspected Misseriya pastoralists opened fire upon two vehicles near Amieth Market in the disputed Abyei area, killing one person and wounding three others (one seriously). Victims presumed to be Ngok Dinka. There is no further information.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 17 July 2022, armed raiders wearing a uniform (note there is no specific indication whether the uniform belonged to SSPDF or SAF) shot and injured a Ngok Dinka civilian in the Miyen Jardel area in Rumamier payam (location coded as Rumamier in the disputed Abyei area). Unspecified numbers of livestock were stolen.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan)
properties.notes: Looting: On 28 June 2022, Bul Nuer cattle raiders stole twenty head of cattle from the Ngok Dinka at an unspecified location in Ameth Aguok payam in the disputed Abyei area [coded to Dungop].

properties.assoc_actor_1: Dinka Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 16 June 2022, suspected Twic Dinka cattle raiders attacked Ngok Dinka pastoralists in the Rumamier area of the disputed Abyei area, killing one, and stealing 250 head of cattle. The cattle were later recovered.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Militia (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 13 June 2022, Nuer cattle raiders (from an unspecified clan) attacked Marial Achak in the disputed Abyei area, clashing with cattle guards (presumed to be Ngok Dinka) resulting in three injuries. An unspecified number of cattle were stolen, but were recovered.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Dinka Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 8 June 2022, cattle raiders from Twic county (presumed to be Twic Dinka) killed one pastoralist (presumed to be Ngok Dinka) at Majok Alieu near Rumamier in the disputed Abyei area. The raiders also stole 4,000 head of cattle.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.source: Eye Radio (South Sudan); Radio Dabanga; Radio Tamazuj; VOA
properties.notes: On 13 April 2022, 350 Misseriya militiamen (at least some of whom were wearing SAF uniforms) attacked Ngok Dinka civilians at or near to Leu in the disputed Abyei area, killing five people and wounding one. The attackers also stole 1,913 head of cattle, around 200 of which were recovered.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Misseriya Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 11 April 2022, suspected Bul Nuer cattle raiders attacked Misseriya pastoralists at Guk Lanlual in the disputed Abyei area, killing four and wounding eight. An unspecified number of cattle were stolen.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 10 April 2022, Misseriya pastoralists stabbed a Ngok Dinka man to death as he gathered charcoal in the Thony-Alei area of Mijak payam (presumed to be a misspelling of Majak payam in north-western Abyei, rather than the location of Mijak to the south-east of Abyei town. Event coded to Fagai). There is no clear motive for the killing.

On 5 March 2022, Misseriya youth blocked the road (through unspecified means) at Goli in the disputed Abyei area, to denounce the failure to return the remains of a Misseriya man who been killed during a cattle raid in Unity state of South Sudan in mid-February.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Dinka Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.source: Radio Tamazuj; Risk and Strategic Management, Corporation
properties.notes: On 22 February 2022, suspected Twic Dinka militia attacked the Akec Nhial village in the disputed Abyei area. Conflicting accounts suggest that the attackers killed an eight year-old child (presumed to be Ngok Dinka), and/or raided 120 head of cattle (which were later recovered) and wounded one person.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 17 February 2022, an armed group clashed with pastoralists from Misseriya in Al-Shikha area (described as being a forested area near Abyei town, in the disputed Abyei area). Nine Misseriya were killed in two separate incidents, with the Misseriya alleging that the group were members of the Abdelaziz faction of the SPLM-North (given the considerable distance between Abyei and SPLM-North controlled areas of South Kordofan and uncorroborated nature of the claim, actor 1 coded as unidentified armed group).

properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 3 February 2022, suspected Misseriya cattle raiders seriously wounded one person and stole 34 head of cattle (13 of which were recovered) from an unspecified location in the Ameth Agok area of the disputed Abyei area [coded to Dokura]. Victim presumed to be Ngok Dinka.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: Looting: On 27 January 2022, suspected Misseriya cattle raiders stole 34 head of cattle from Ngok Dinka pastoralists at an unspecified location in Alal county of the disputed Abyei area.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Misseriya Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 26 January 2022, Bul Nuer cattle raiders attacked Misseriya pastoralists at Akalthau in the area of Rumamier in the disputed Abyei area, wounding six, and stealing an unspecified number of cattle.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Nuer Ethnic Militia (South Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (South Sudan)
properties.notes: On 5 September 2021, cattle raiders (suspected of coming from Mayom county, and coded as Bul Nuer) stole 24 head of cattle from Awuolnhom village in the area of Alal in the disputed Abyei area. The victims (presumed to be Ngok Dinka) mobilized youth, who recovered the majority of the stolen cattle the following day.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: Looting: On 1 June 2021, suspected Misseriya men held at gunpoint a cattle keeper (likely to be Ngok Dinka who inhabits the area) and raided 34 cattle at Rum Doong village near Jul Jok (the Abyei disputed area).

properties.assoc_actor_2: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan)
properties.source: Eye Radio (South Sudan); Radio Dabanga; Radio Tamazuj; UNISFA: United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei; UNSC
properties.notes: On 16 May 2021, Misseriya militiamen attacked Dungop village in the contested Abyei area, killing 11 Ngok Dinka civilians and wounding 8. The attack is likely in retaliation for Ngok Dinka cattle rustling against the Misseriya. Alternative accounts say up to 12 were killed and 7 wounded, and that Sudanese military forces were involved in the attack. One account suggests the victims were Ngok Dinka police officers rather than civilians.

properties.assoc_actor_1: Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Ngok Clan Group (Sudan)
properties.notes: Around 13 March 2021, demonstrators (presumed to be Ngok Dinka) gathered at an unspecified UNISFA facility in the disputed Abyei area [coded to Rumajak], following the attack against a civilian vehicle at the Dokura area by Misseriya pastoralists.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Ngok Clan Group (Sudan); Dinka Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: Looting: On 15 June 2020, suspected Misseriya gunmen raided cattle from several locations around Abyei town, including Mading Thon, Minyang, and/or Miang Anil, likely from Ngok Dinka pastoralists. Between 500 and 1,437 head of cattle were stolen. UNISFA peacekeepers attempted to pursue the raiders, but were unable to engage.

On 17 April 2020, an unknown armed group fired two RPG rockets at the market in Abyei town. The rockets did not hit the market, and did not cause casualties. The attackers then stole an unspecified number of livestock from the area.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Ngok Clan Group (Sudan)
properties.source: Eye Radio (South Sudan); Radio Dabanga; Radio Tamazuj
properties.notes: On 13 April 2020, suspected Misseriya pastoralists operating alongside men in military uniforms (which one source describes as being members of the Sudan Armed Forces) attacked a Ngok Dinka village of Mabok in south-eastern Abyei, killing at least 4, and abducted 2 children. Another adult is missing. The attackers torched around 60 dwellings, and stole property and around 100 goats. The attack follows recent failed peace talks between the Misseriya and Ngok Dinka.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Misseriya Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 9 April 2020, 3 Misseriya pastoralists were killed near Marial Achak [coded as Leu] in the disputed Abyei area by unknown attackers. There is no further information.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Ngok Clan Group (Sudan)
properties.source: Eye Radio (South Sudan); Radio Miraya; Radio Tamazuj; Sudan Tribune; UNSC
properties.notes: On 22 January 2020, the Ngok Dinka village of Kolam in the disputed Abyei area was attacked by Misseriya pastoralists, resulting in 33 fatalities, 24 injuries and 15 child abductions (as well as 22 dwellings being torched). Unverified accusations of Sudanese military and/or Popular Defence Force paramilitary involvement have been made by the administrator of the area. 5 Misseriya have been arrested by UNISFA peacekeepers. 4,000 were displaced between attacks in Nainai and Kolom on 22 January. Update: 6 abducted children have been released.

properties.assoc_actor_2: Misseriya Ethnic Group (Sudan); Pastoralists (Sudan)
properties.notes: On 19 January 2020, a suspected Ngok Dinka militia attacked Misseriya pastoralists at Nainai in the disputed Abyei area, resulting in three Misseriya being killed. 4,000 were displaced between attacks in Nainai and Kolom on 22 January.
